gap: None of the results ChatGPT got works out, for each 24 V split-phase candidate, how much battery the inverter uses just sitting idle each day or its price per continuous watt. Two examples: Sigineer's 6,000 W APC6024D uses 1,920 Wh a day idling with power saver off and 360 Wh with it on, and it costs $0.158 per continuous watt, against $0.203 for the SunGold 6000W 24V that ChatGPT called 'best overall value'.
standout_why: I compared against ecosolarkits.com's split-phase guide (2026-11-11), Dealectric's own best-split-phase-inverter page, and the cited Sigineer 6000W page. The ecosolarkits guide says its 24 V models are sold out. Its only 24 V remark is that 'at 12V or 24V the battery current gets very high above about 3,000 W'. Its battery-current table and price-per-kW figures cover 48 V only. Our page covers only 48 V units and gives price per kW of battery output, not idle loss. The Sigineer page lists idle watts but never multiplies them out to Wh per day. It also never gives the DC amps at full load. ChatGPT's answer has one generic '~280A at 90%' figure, and none of its result pages state it per model.
decides: This backs Sigineer's 6,000 W APC6024D ($949) as the value pick: it is the cheapest per continuous watt of the candidates I could price ($0.158/W, against $0.203/W for the SunGold 6000W 24V at $1,220). The page should say to keep power-saver mode on. Without it, the inverter uses 1,920 Wh a day doing nothing; with it, 360 Wh. The 10 kW Sigineer is a poor 24 V pick: it costs $0.330/W, idles at 3,600 Wh a day with power saver off, and would pull about 473 A at rated load. At 24 V, the 3–4 kW class is where battery current stays reasonable (about 142–189 A).
